To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
social media use is associated with body image dissatisfaction and disordered eating in adolescent females.
social media use is associated with body image in adolescents, and that social comparison is a possible mediator.

1) the impact of social network sites on body image is mixed, 2) the effect of social network sites is moderated by gender, 3) social comparison is a mechanism that links the use of social network sites to body image, and 4) the impact of body image on social network site use is mediated by appearance-based self-views.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of SNS on body image and body image concerns in adolescents.
the impact of social networking sites on body image and self-esteem.
the impact of social networking sites (Sns) on body image and body dissatisfaction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the impact of social networking sites and the practice of selfie taking on body image in young people remains inconclusive.
social media is having a negative impact on the body image of adolescents and young adults.
social media has both positive and negative effects on body image.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that social media use is linked to body image concerns, but not body image disturbance (e.g., body dissatisfaction, drive for thinness, and bulimic symptoms).
social media has a positive impact on body image.
the use of SNS and taking selfies can have a detrimental impact on body image.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of social media is not a cause for body image concerns and that it is important to consider other risk factors when assessing the impact of SNS.

we need to be aware that the social comparison processes that have been linked to body dissatisfaction in offline contexts are also occurring online and that the social comparison process is not necessarily the only way that social media use can influence body image.
social media use can be associated with body dissatisfaction in some individuals, but not in others, and that this may depend on a range of factors.
